points.description: States that a static array keeps/retains its values (persists, has static storage duration) for the whole program run / between function calls, rather than being re-created each call. Accept 'lifetime is the entire program' or 'value is preserved between calls'.

levels.says: Vague hint at persistence (e.g. 'exists longer', 'stays in memory') without saying values are kept between calls or lifetime is the whole program.

points.description: States that a static array is initialized only once (at compile time/program start or the first time the function runs), whereas a non-static (automatic/local) array is re-initialized every time the function is called/block entered. Model answer's statement 'initialized only once' earns this.

levels.says: Says static array is initialized only once but does not contrast with non-static being re-initialized each call.

points.description: States that a non-static (automatic) local array is created on entry to the function/block (usually on the stack) and destroyed on exit, so its contents are lost/undefined between calls.

levels.says: Says only that non-static array is local or temporary without stating it is destroyed/lost on exit or recreated per call.

points.description: Mentions an additional valid difference: static arrays are stored in the static/data segment (not the stack) and, if not explicitly initialized, are zero-initialized by default, whereas non-static local arrays hold garbage/indeterminate values if uninitialized. Either fact earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks need: static array persists across calls and is initialized once, contrasted with non-static arrays being recreated, reinitialized and lost each call. The model answer alone (initialized once) earns roughly 2 of 5 here, giving credit for the core idea; contrast and persistence are needed for more. Wrong claims (e.g. static arrays can't be modified) earn nothing for that point.
rubric.answer_key: A static array has static storage duration: it is allocated once (in the static/data segment), initialized only once (zero-filled by default if no initializer), and keeps its values for the whole program run, including between function calls. A non-static (automatic) local array is created each time the function/block is entered (on the stack), re-initialized each call, holds garbage if not initialized, and is destroyed when the function exits, so its contents are lost.
